position_summary: Opposes the 2025-26 Trump tariff regime as a cost on Ohio farmers and consumers, while keeping a long protectionist record that supported some tariffs in the past.
candidate_statement: "Farmers can't afford a new tractor or a new combine. They in many cases can't even afford spare parts because of the tariffs." (Cleveland.com, 2026-11-13); the Dispatch issue survey records that "Brown and Redpath oppose Trump's tariffs".
context: Post-election interview and the Columbus Dispatch candidate issue survey.
legislative_record: Voted against NAFTA; supported the 2018 washing-machine tariffs and USMCA; author of 'Myths of Free Trade' (2006) — per Wikipedia biography.
change_notes: A pro-tariff legislator in 2018 who campaigned in 2026 against the tariffs in force. The archive records the shift without adjudicating it.
opponent_criticism: Husted's spokesperson said Husted backs "boosting access to foreign markets" while ensuring Ohio businesses are treated fairly.
fact_check: The $11 billion / $2,200-per-household cost figure in the Dispatch survey is attributed to the National Taxpayers Union Foundation, an advocacy group, not an official estimate.

subissue: unions, UAW and the right to organize
position_summary: Union-first campaign built on endorsements from the UAW, Steelworkers, IUPAT, IFPTE, CWA, the Ohio Federation of Teachers and the Ohio AFL-CIO; pledges to co-sponsor the Faster Labor Contracts Act.
candidate_statement: Teamsters endorsement release: Brown "introduced the bipartisan Railway Safety Act" and "has committed to co-sponsoring the Faster Labor Contracts Act in the Senate".
context: Ohio Conference of Teamsters 2026 endorsement release.
legislative_record: Railway Safety Act (bipartisan, with JD Vance, 2023); pension protection for Teamsters retirees; Senate Banking Committee chair 2021-2025.
change_notes: Consistent labor alignment across the cycle.
opponent_criticism: Husted campaign argues Brown's long tenure produced no wage gains; Husted: "he's been in office for over 50 years".
fact_check: Endorsement claims are sponsor-stated; the Railway Safety Act's failure in the Senate is documented in the Wikipedia JD Vance article.

position_summary: Pitches an Ohio manufacturing revival and frames productivity gains as captured by corporations rather than wages.
candidate_statement: "Ohio workers are more productive than ever, but no matter how hard they work, their pay doesn't keep up." (statement to the Columbus Dispatch, published 2026-10-18).
context: Dispatch candidate issue survey.
legislative_record: Championed the Dignity of Work Institute after leaving the Senate (2025-03-25); no 2026 legislative record (not in office during the race).
opponent_criticism: Husted credits Trump-era tariff protection with Kenworth adding 1,000 jobs in Chillicothe and calls that "the America First agenda".
fact_check: The 1,000-job Kenworth figure is the Husted campaign's own claim as quoted by Cleveland.com; not independently confirmed in this archive.

position_summary: Pro-choice; campaigned with abortion-rights groups in a state whose constitution has protected abortion since Issue 1 (2023).
candidate_statement: no verbatim statement retrieved in this archive
context: No 2026 Brown statement on abortion was retrieved; the position is inferred from endorsements and the state context, which is why it is marked partially verified.
legislative_record: Senate record includes support for codifying Roe; not re-verified from a primary document in this archive.
opponent_criticism: Husted attacked the abortion pill in a Senate hearing and cited his own adoption story; he did not contest Issue 1 in this race.
fact_check: Issue 1 (2023-11-07) passed 57%-43% per Wikipedia.

position_summary: Supports restricting gun access for people with criminal records or mental-health issues; endorsed by Giffords.
candidate_statement: WLWT reports Brown supports "restricting gun access for certain people with criminal records and mental-health issues".
context: WLWT sit-down published with the result coverage.
legislative_record: Giffords endorsement (2025-09-18); Senate votes not re-verified here.
opponent_criticism: No Husted gun-policy attack retrieved.
fact_check: not applicable

position_summary: Supports deporting immigrants convicted of serious crimes, extending TPS for Springfield's Haitian community, and a legalization path for long-resident taxpayers.
candidate_statement: "I, of course, support deportation of those people who have committed a serious crime... Beyond that, I want to see us work out a real policy on immigration where people who have been in this country and worked hard and paid their taxes can continue to contribute to society." (reporters, August 2026, quoted by the Dispatch).
context: Dispatch issue survey; OCJ also reports Brown pressing DeWine and Ohio's senators on TPS.
legislative_record: Opposed the 2025 executive order on sanctuary jurisdictions; backed fentanyl-trafficking and human-smuggling penalties and border technology funding (per the Dispatch survey).
opponent_criticism: Husted: "Why do people like Sherrod Brown care more about people who are illegally in this country than he cares about you?"
fact_check: The Dispatch attributes the legislative record summary to the campaigns' own descriptions.

position_summary: Wants data centers to pay for their own power and opposes "out-of-control tax giveaways"; makes Husted's data-center recruitment the centre of his closing argument.
candidate_statement: "Husted's been the front guy on all these data centers, 200 in Ohio, getting huge over-the-top tax breaks, and raising utility rates." (Ohio Capital Journal interview, 2026-08-21)
context: OCJ story on the leaked NRSC memo.
legislative_record: No 2026 legislative record; position expressed in ads and interviews.
change_notes: Brown applauded Amazon's central-Ohio data center in a 2015 release (per the Dispatch survey) — a documented earlier position.
opponent_criticism: Husted says data centers bring jobs and money to rural Ohio; DeWine defends them as economic development.
fact_check: The "200 in Ohio" figure is Brown's own count, not an official tally.

position_summary: Frames environmental protection as an Ohio jobs and public-health issue; endorsed by the League of Conservation Voters Action Fund.
candidate_statement: "When Norfolk Southern's negligence contaminated East Palestine, I was there from day one holding them accountable and securing federal resources." (LCV endorsement release)
context: LCV Action Fund endorsement.
legislative_record: Lead-paint and lead-pipe remediation work; Great Lakes protection, per the same release.
opponent_criticism: Husted blames Brown for "radical environmental policies that closed 23 power plants in the state" (Boardman rally, 2026-10-15).
fact_check: The 23-plant figure is Husted's claim at a rally; not verified here.

position_summary: Author of the bipartisan Railway Safety Act introduced after the 2023-02-03 Norfolk Southern derailment; returns to the derailment as a accountability story.
candidate_statement: "I want to see rail safety legislation passed in the next few weeks." (East Palestine press briefing, 2023-02-27, recorded by Wikipedia)
context: East Palestine derailment response — pre-campaign record.
legislative_record: Railway Safety Act co-sponsored with JD Vance (2023-03-01); the bill did not pass.
change_notes: Position unchanged; the bill's failure is the record.
opponent_criticism: No Husted attack on Brown's rail record retrieved.
fact_check: Bill failure documented in the Wikipedia JD Vance article.

position_summary: Attacks the lapse of enhanced ACA subsidies and the coverage losses that followed; frames health costs as an affordability issue.
candidate_statement: "These hospitals are a lifeline for their communities, especially for low-income families... This will continue to be a priority for me in the Senate." (Dispatch survey, on rural hospitals)
context: Dispatch issue survey.
legislative_record: Senate record includes ACA defense; not re-verified from a primary document here.
opponent_criticism: Husted says Brown and Democrats "created the broken ACA system" and offers a two-year subsidy extension with a $5 monthly payment.
fact_check: Around 161,000 Ohioans lost or dropped coverage Feb 2025-Feb 2026 per the Dispatch survey (source not named in the retrieved text).

subissue: tax law and child tax credit
position_summary: Calls the 2025 tax law tilted to high earners; backs restoring the expanded child tax credit.
candidate_statement: "...cutting taxes for working families, not billionaires and corporations." (statement to the Dispatch, 2026-10-18)
context: Dispatch issue survey.
legislative_record: Not in office in 2026; no vote on the 2025 law.
opponent_criticism: Husted backed the law and cites a projected $3,173 average saving for Ohioans (Tax Foundation estimate).
fact_check: The $3,173 figure is a Tax Foundation estimate cited by the Husted campaign, not an official score.

position_summary: Opposes benefit cuts; discusses solvency fixes at a joint appearance with Husted.
candidate_statement: no verbatim statement retrieved in this archive
context: OCJ reports the two candidates discussed how to fix Social Security on 2026-10-12; the retrieved summary does not quote Brown verbatim.
legislative_record: Senate record not re-verified here.
opponent_criticism: unknown
fact_check: not applicable

subissue: voting rules and the SAVE Act
position_summary: Opposes new federal proof-of-citizenship and photo-ID mandates; defends early, mail and Election Day voting.
candidate_statement: "We want to make sure that Ohioans' votes are counted, which means allowing folks to vote early, mail in their ballots and vote on Election Day." (Dispatch survey, 2026-10-18)
context: Dispatch issue survey; Brown did not address the SAVE America Act directly.
legislative_record: Former Ohio secretary of state (1983-1991).
opponent_criticism: Husted is a staunch SAVE Act supporter and pushed a standalone photo-ID measure.
fact_check: The Dispatch notes Brown "didn't directly address the legislation".

position_summary: Makes record outside spending the explicit villain of his closing argument.
candidate_statement: "Corporations and billionaires may try to buy this election for their golden boy, Jon Husted. But there are more of us than there are of them." (Cleveland.com, 2026-10-31)
context: Closing-argument reporting.
legislative_record: Endorsed by End Citizens United (2026-05-12).
opponent_criticism: Husted's side argues the spending is independent expenditure, not campaign money.
fact_check: Total race spending exceeds $500 million per Cleveland.com — an estimate, not an FEC total.

position_summary: Calls for ending the war with Iran as an inflation and gas-price measure.
candidate_statement: Brown "rants against Trump's war with Iran" on the trail (The Guardian, 2026-11-03) and says ending the war would help lower prices (WLWT, 2026-11-02).
context: Result coverage and the WLWT sit-down.
legislative_record: Senate foreign-policy votes not re-verified here.
opponent_criticism: Brown criticises Husted's votes to continue the war; Husted's own rationale was not retrieved.
fact_check: OCJ (2026-03-05) found no Ohio Senate candidate gave unqualified support to the war — including Brown.

position_summary: Opposes corporate-controlled surveillance; wants more facts before regulating.
candidate_statement: Brown called Flock cameras "another example of corporations taking control over our communities" (Dispatch survey, 2026-10-18).
context: Dispatch issue survey.
legislative_record: No record retrieved.
opponent_criticism: Husted would consider regulating camera placement near national-security sites.
fact_check: not applicable

position_summary: Does not repudiate the tariff regime; frames the answer as market access, predictability and anti-transshipment enforcement.
candidate_statement: "Ohio relies on the relationship with trading partners like Canada, but it's got to be fair... They want predictability, but they also don't want to have China using countries like Canada to import products into Canada and then moving them into America." (reporters, August 2026)
context: Dispatch issue survey; the campaign says Husted supports "boosting access to foreign markets".
legislative_record: No Senate trade vote retrieved.
opponent_criticism: Brown says the tariffs raise grocery and equipment costs and that Husted won't break with Trump on them.
fact_check: The campaign's phrasing is reported through spokesperson Amy Natoce; no Husted quote endorsing the tariffs was retrieved.

position_summary: Credits tariff protection and permitting reform with Ohio manufacturing wins; makes Chillicothe's Kenworth expansion his proof point.
candidate_statement: "Protecting American manufacturing is the America First agenda." (post on X, quoted by Cleveland.com, 2026-10-31)
context: Closing-argument reporting; the Kenworth claim precedes the 2026-10-28 Chillicothe rally.
legislative_record: Permitting-reform bill for energy infrastructure (per the campaign).
opponent_criticism: Brown calls the manufacturing message a cover for corporate tax breaks.
fact_check: The 1,000-job Kenworth figure is campaign-stated; not independently confirmed here.

position_summary: Defends the 2025 tax law and sponsors a bill to smooth the "benefits cliff" for people leaving assistance.
candidate_statement: no verbatim statement retrieved in this archive
context: Dispatch survey describes his support and the benefits-cliff bill without quoting him directly.
legislative_record: Backed the 2025 law (no tax on tips/overtime, higher child tax credit, work requirements); sponsoring the benefits-cliff pilot bill.
opponent_criticism: Brown says the law prioritises high earners.
fact_check: The $3,173 average saving is a Tax Foundation estimate cited by the campaign.

position_summary: Carries endorsements from the Operating Engineers, Boilermakers, ABC of Ohio, the Cleveland Building Trades, the FOP and the Teamsters' rival building-trades wing — an unusual Republican labour footprint.
candidate_statement: no verbatim statement retrieved in this archive
context: Endorsement releases and Wikipedia's endorsement list.
legislative_record: No labour bill retrieved.
opponent_criticism: Brown's campaign presents the UAW/Steelworkers endorsements as the real labour verdict.
fact_check: Endorsement claims are sponsor-stated.

position_summary: Opposes expanded access to the abortion pill; opposes abortion generally and uses his own adoption story.
candidate_statement: At a Senate HELP Committee hearing Husted "spoke against the abortion pill" and "pointed to his own adoption story, in which he said his mother could have chosen abortion" (OCJ, 2026-01-22).
context: Senate HELP Committee hearing, 'protecting women against dangerous abortion drugs'.
legislative_record: Committee participation only; no bill retrieved.
opponent_criticism: Ohio voters protected abortion in Issue 1 (2023); Brown's side uses that against him.
fact_check: OCJ reports decades of research showing mifepristone is safe and severe complications rare — a counterweight to the hearing's premise.

position_summary: Supports the Trump immigration agenda and says immigration law "should be implemented as it was intended", including TPS and birthright citizenship.
candidate_statement: "Ohio families deserve a fighter in the U.S. Senate who will put their safety and well-being first, and stand up for the rule of law – not with dangerous criminals." (spokesperson Amy Natoce, Dispatch survey)
context: Dispatch issue survey; the candidate statement is issued through his spokesperson.
legislative_record: No immigration bill retrieved.
opponent_criticism: Brown calls the crackdown chaotic and defends Springfield's Haitian community.
fact_check: The Dispatch notes ICE has detained people with no criminal record, contradicting the 'criminals' framing.

position_summary: Defends data centers as rural jobs and money; sponsors a bill requiring regulators to consider a large-load cost-allocation blueprint without mandating it.
candidate_statement: No verbatim statement retrieved; the Dispatch survey describes the bill and the campaign's permitting-reform argument.
context: Dispatch issue survey; OCJ documents his recruitment of data centers as lieutenant governor.
legislative_record: Bill requiring state regulators to consider a policy blueprint making large-load data centers pay for their power.
change_notes: Earlier in 2026 he said data centers need to be more responsible (OCJ); the bill is the later, weaker instrument.
opponent_criticism: Brown calls him the "face of data centers" and blames him for utility bills; the NRSC memo calls data centers "the anchor hanging around Husted's neck".
fact_check: The Plain Dealer nickname "Face of Data Centers" is reported by Wikipedia citing the Plain Dealer.

position_summary: Wants a two-year extension of enhanced ACA tax credits paired with a $5 minimum monthly payment to deter fraud.
candidate_statement: "Husted was not in Congress when Sherrod Brown and Democrats created the broken ACA system... but he has worked to be part of a thoughtful solution" (spokesperson Amy Natoce, Dispatch survey).
context: Dispatch issue survey.
legislative_record: Introduced the two-year extension bill; backed the OTC-drug streamlining law.
change_notes: In December 2025 he wanted to "freeze" the subsidies (OCJ); by October 2026 he sponsored a two-year extension.
opponent_criticism: Brown says the conditions would raise costs for poor enrollees.
fact_check: The $5 minimum payment is described by the campaign as an anti-fraud measure; no independent analysis retrieved.

position_summary: Claims the $50 billion rural-hospital fund as a win and calls it the most consequential rural-health step in years.
candidate_statement: Spokesperson Natoce called the rural hospital funding "one of the most consequential steps that Congress has taken to support rural health care in years" (Dispatch survey).
context: Dispatch issue survey.
legislative_record: Supported the 2025 law's $50 billion rural hospital fund; Ohio received more than $200 million per DeWine's office.
opponent_criticism: Brown says the money does not offset the Medicaid cuts.
fact_check: The $200 million Ohio figure is attributed to DeWine's office.

subissue: SAVE America Act and photo ID
position_summary: Staunch supporter of the SAVE America Act and of a standalone photo-ID measure; as a former secretary of state he owns the issue.
candidate_statement: Husted recorded Senate floor remarks on requiring photo identification to vote on 2026-07-27 (Commons audio file description).
context: Senate floor; the Wikipedia infobox links the recording.
legislative_record: Pushed the Senate to consider a standalone photo-ID measure.
opponent_criticism: Brown says the push sows distrust and would suppress voting.
fact_check: The Dispatch notes the Senate remains deadlocked on the SAVE Act.

position_summary: Long record of expanding school choice, charter schools and religious education access in Ohio.
candidate_statement: no verbatim statement retrieved in this archive
context: Wikipedia biography and its cited NBC4 piece.
legislative_record: State legislative record: income-tax cut and school-choice expansion as Speaker (2005-2009).
opponent_criticism: No 2026 Brown attack on school choice retrieved.
fact_check: State-record claims come from a Wikipedia citation of The Daily Advocate (2007) and NBC4 (2026).

position_summary: Favours progressively replacing human jobs with AI and wants to attract the data-center build-out that underpins it.
candidate_statement: Wikipedia, citing the Plain Dealer: "During the 2026 campaign, he favored progressively replacing human jobs with AI."
context: Campaign-period position recorded in the biography.
legislative_record: No AI bill retrieved.
opponent_criticism: Brown's data-center attack is the closest surrogate for an AI critique; no direct AI attack retrieved.
fact_check: The claim rests on a single Wikipedia sentence citing the Plain Dealer; the Plain Dealer article itself was not retrieved, so the exact wording is unconfirmed.

position_summary: Voted to continue the Iran war (as characterised by Brown); supported Russia sanctions in 2025 unless Moscow pursued a lasting peace.
candidate_statement: no verbatim statement retrieved in this archive
context: Wikipedia biography (Russia sanctions) and Cleveland.com (Iran votes).
legislative_record: 2025 Russia sanctions support; Iran war votes.
opponent_criticism: Brown: "criticizes Husted's votes to continue the war in Iran".
fact_check: OCJ found no Ohio Senate candidate gave unqualified support to the war; Husted's precise position was not retrieved.

position_summary: Runs as the appointed incumbent, dating his tenure to the 2025-01-17 announcement and the 2025-01-21 oath; his opponents call the seat "unelected".
candidate_statement: "We have worked to make Ohio great again, and I look forward to working with President Trump and JD Vance to make America great again." (appointment remarks, 2025-01-17, OCJ)
context: DeWine's appointment announcement at the Ohio Statehouse.
legislative_record: Appointed by Gov. Mike DeWine on 2025-01-17; sworn in 2025-01-21.
opponent_criticism: OCJ commentary notes the Husted campaign trying to cast Brown as the incumbent; Brown calls him a special interest insider.
fact_check: The brief's dates (appointed 2025-01-10, sworn in 2025-01-14) are wrong: 2025-01-10 is Vance's resignation date; the appointment was announced 2025-01-17 and the oath administered 2025-01-21.
